hypotheses.claim: A failed troubleshoot submit that the SE retries creates TWO submission rows, because the mobile form mints a fresh clientSubmissionId on every tap instead of once per form session.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The id is stabilised outside the handler — a useState/useRef/useMemo seed, or the api client itself dedupes retries.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -n 'clientSubmissionId|randomUUID|useRef|useMemo' apps/mobile/src/tickets/troubleshoot/TroubleshootFormScreen.tsx — the only hit is line 56, inline in handleSubmit; no useRef/useMemo in the file, and grep -n 'randomUUID' apps/mobile/src/api/client.ts is empty.

hypotheses.claim: A component request raised from the SE's component-unavailable toggle reaches the Warehouse Manager with componentId NULL, so nobody can tell what part to ship.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The WM screen resolves the part some other way — from the ticket's expected components, or the SE picks the item on a later screen.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -n 'componentUnavailableItem' across apps/mobile/src and apps/backend/src/ticketing — declared in the service input (:37) and written (:231) but never populated by any caller; the controller body map at troubleshoot.controller.ts:26 carries componentUnavailable only.

hypotheses.claim: Filing and resuming a Vehicle Unavailability report stops and restarts the primary SLA clock with zero audit_log row, so an SLA pause cannot be attributed to an actor.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: Audit is written by a shared helper the two methods call (foldAndResumeSlaPause), or by an interceptor, not in the method body.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -n 'withAudit|auditLog.create|audit.record' apps/backend/src/ticketing/vehicle-unavailability.service.ts returns exactly one hit, :374 (approve/override/confirm-date path); fileReport's $transaction body (:147-219) and resumeSla's (:439-456) contain none.

hypotheses.claim: The Shadow Use reassurance line on the 409 Conflict screen is dead code over HTTP: shadowUseRecorded is always false because the request DTO carries no consumedComponents.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: Consumed components are inferred server-side from the SE's van stock or the ticket's expected components rather than sent by the client.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'consumedComponents' apps/backend/src/ticketing apps/mobile/src/api/client.ts packages/shared/src — only the service input type (:39), its two read sites (:296, :330) and a shared-types comment at packages/shared/src/index.ts:468 naming it a structural gap; no producer anywhere.

hypotheses.claim: An SE can open a shared-pool ticket detail they are not assigned to, but the same SE is blocked from every write route on it, so the read surface promises work the app will refuse.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: Shared-pool reads only ever surface TROUBLESHOOT tickets, whose submit path deliberately drops the assignment requirement, so no promise is broken.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -n 'isAssignedSe|coverage floor|assignment is not required' across recovery.service.ts, install-lifecycle.service.ts and troubleshoot-submission.service.ts — troubleshoot waives assignment (:121 comment) while recovery/install both hard-gate on isAssignedSe, and se-ticket-access.ts:32 applies one shared-pool predicate to all three work types.
